description: Inspection, sanitisation, accessibility, proofing and release-gate policy for the word-document-agent skill tool. Edit this file to change what 'inspect', 'sanitize', 'a11y', 'proof' and 'qa' consider a problem. Every rule id is reported verbatim in structured output so downstream skills can map it to their own vocabulary.

targets.why: Author names travel with the file and identify the machine's owner.
The last editor is personal metadata.
Custom properties frequently store ticket, customer or project identifiers.
Comment bodies and authors are internal review data.
Unaccepted revisions keep deleted text recoverable inside the file.
Hidden text is invisible on screen but present in the file.
White text is a common way to hide content; removal needs human judgement.
OLE objects and packages carry full external files.
Custom XML blobs may contain source data that never shows on the page.
Macro removal changes file type; do it deliberately, never silently.
External targets reveal internal URLs and file server paths.
GUID identifiers tie copies of a document together.

rules.why: Screen readers announce the document title; it must be set.
Proofing and screen-reader pronunciation depend on the document language.
Skipped heading levels break the outline used by assistive technology.
Long documents without heading styles have no navigable structure.
Images without alternative text are unreadable to screen readers.
Link text such as 'click here' is meaningless when read out of context.
Data tables need a repeating header row so readers keep column meaning.
A blank header cell leaves a column unlabelled.
Ragged tables are ambiguous when read cell by cell.
Hidden text is invisible but still read by assistive technology in some paths.
Meaning carried only by colour is lost in mono print and to colour-blind readers.
Text smaller than 8 pt is hard to read.
An empty heading creates a dead entry in the navigation pane.
Content controls without a title/tag are announced as unknown fields.
No outline means no table-of-contents or navigation support.

checks.why: Template placeholders left in a released document are visible defects.
Authoring markers must not reach recipients.
Repeated words are the most common typo after editing.
Double spaces inside sentences create uneven spacing in justified text.
Straight quotes look mechanical in typographic documents.
Trailing spaces change line breaks and break copy-paste.
Space before punctuation is a frequent paste artefact.
Runs of empty paragraphs indicate layout made with Enter instead of spacing.

qa_gate.notes: Set fail_on_severity to [] for an advisory-only gate; 'qa --report-only' overrides severity handling at run time.
